title: Comparison of the effects of real-life cue exposure (CE) to a standardized virtual reality (VR) cue exposure and to a VR-CE individualized using artificial intelligence on cue-induced alcohol craving
summary:
Excessive alcohol consumption is a serious global health issue, with intense craving for alcohol playing a central role. Such cravings are often triggered by specific environments or cues—for example, being in a bar.
In therapy, these situations can be deliberately recreated to help individuals practice managing their cravings. These so-called cue exposure techniques aim to reduce cue reactivity over time and prevent relapse.
However, such exposures in clinical settings are often far removed from everyday life. Virtual reality (VR) offers a promising alternative, enabling realistic, cost-effective, and flexible representations of various situations. Artificial intelligence (AI) can further personalize these virtual environments—for instance, by selecting relevant cues or adjusting difficulty in real time.
So far, VR-based approaches have rarely been compared to real-life situations, and the potential of AI in this context remains largely unexplored. Therefore, in our current study, we aim to investigate the effects of virtual cue exposure in comparison to real-life cue exposure on cue-induced alcohol craving.

interventions.name: Six-armed randomized controlled cross-over study comparing the effects of three different cue-exposure conditions at different time points: A – alcohol cue exposure in a BarLab setting; B – alcohol cue exposure in a standardized virtual reality setting; C – alcohol cue exposure in an AI-personalized

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Diagnosis of an alcohol use disorder (AUD) according to the DSM-5 (i.e. meeting >= 2 criteria)
• Ability of the individual to understand the character and the individual consequences of the study
• Capacity to provide written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
• Current psychotic or bipolar disorder or current severe depressive episode with suicidal ideations
• Any withdrawal symptoms at the time of the study visit (CIWA score >3)
• Breath alcohol concentration > 0.0 at the time of the study visit
• Positive drug screening (amphetamines/ecstasy, opiates, cocaine, barbiturates, cannabis, psychotropic drugs)
• Severe comorbidities and/or complications that demand invasive surgery and/or intensive care
• Acute suicidal tendency or acute endangerment of self and others
